# HelpChatbot Implementation Plan

## Problem
Build a web-based, LLM-driven customer help chatbot using C#/Blazor with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over internal product PDF documentation. Uses Postgres for data storage and a local `Docs/` folder for PDF files.

## Approach
Use **Microsoft.Extensions.AI** (the official .NET AI abstraction) with **Blazor Server** for the UI and **pgvector** in Postgres for vector similarity search. PDFs are ingested at startup, chunked, embedded, and stored in Postgres. User questions are answered by retrieving relevant chunks and passing them as context to the LLM.

## Architecture

```
[Blazor Server UI] → [ChatService] → [EmbeddingService] → Postgres/pgvector
                                    → [LLM via Microsoft.Extensions.AI]
                                    → [PdfIngestionService] ← Docs/*.pdf
```

## Key NuGet Packages
- `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI` — LLM + embeddings (works with OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or any compatible endpoint)
- `UglyToad.PdfPig` — PDF text extraction
- `Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL` — Postgres via EF Core
- `Pgvector.EntityFrameworkCore` — pgvector support for EF Core

## Todos

### 1. Project setup & dependencies
- Add NuGet packages to `HelpChatbot.csproj`
- Add `appsettings.json` with connection string and AI endpoint config

### 2. Data model & EF Core context
- `DocumentChunk` entity: Id, FileName, ChunkIndex, Content, Embedding (vector)
- `ChatMessage` entity: Id, SessionId, Role, Content, Timestamp
- `AppDbContext` with pgvector extension enabled on migration

### 3. PDF ingestion service
- Read all PDFs from `Docs/` folder using PdfPig
- Split text into ~500-token overlapping chunks
- Generate embeddings via `IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>`
- Upsert chunks into Postgres (skip if file already ingested)

### 4. RAG retrieval service
- Accept a user query, embed it, perform cosine similarity search against `DocumentChunk` table
- Return top-K most relevant chunks

### 5. Chat service
- Maintain conversation history per session (stored in Postgres)
- Build a system prompt with retrieved context chunks
- Stream LLM responses via `IChatClient`

### 6. Blazor Server UI
- Chat page (`Components/Pages/Chat.razor`) with message bubbles, input box, send button
- Streaming response display
- Basic CSS styling (clean, minimal)

### 7. Program.cs wiring
- Register services (EF Core, ChatService, PdfIngestionService, AI clients)
- Configure Blazor Server
- Trigger PDF ingestion on startup

### 8. Database migration
- Add initial EF Core migration
- Auto-apply on startup

## Notes
- The LLM provider is configurable via `appsettings.json` — works with OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible API (Ollama, etc.)
- PDF ingestion runs once at startup; re-ingests only new/changed files
- Chat history is persisted per session ID (browser session)
- pgvector handles vector storage and similarity search natively in Postgres

# HelpChatbot Implementation Plan

## Problem
Build a web-based, LLM-driven customer help chatbot using C#/Blazor with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over internal product PDF documentation. Uses Postgres for data storage and a local `Docs/` folder for PDF files.

## Approach
Use **Microsoft.Extensions.AI** (the official .NET AI abstraction) with **Blazor Server** for the UI and **pgvector** in Postgres for vector similarity search. PDFs are ingested at startup, chunked, embedded, and stored in Postgres. User questions are answered by retrieving relevant chunks and passing them as context to the LLM.

## Architecture

```
[Blazor Server UI] → [ChatService] → [EmbeddingService] → Postgres/pgvector
                                    → [LLM via Microsoft.Extensions.AI]
                                    → [PdfIngestionService] ← Docs/*.pdf
```

## Key NuGet Packages
- `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI` — LLM + embeddings (works with OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or any compatible endpoint)
- `UglyToad.PdfPig` — PDF text extraction
- `Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL` — Postgres via EF Core
- `Pgvector.EntityFrameworkCore` — pgvector support for EF Core

## Todos

### 1. Project setup & dependencies
- Add NuGet packages to `HelpChatbot.csproj`
- Add `appsettings.json` with connection string and AI endpoint config

### 2. Data model & EF Core context
- `DocumentChunk` entity: Id, FileName, ChunkIndex, Content, Embedding (vector)
- `ChatMessage` entity: Id, SessionId, Role, Content, Timestamp
- `AppDbContext` with pgvector extension enabled on migration

### 3. PDF ingestion service
- Read all PDFs from `Docs/` folder using PdfPig
- Split text into ~500-token overlapping chunks
- Generate embeddings via `IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>`
- Upsert chunks into Postgres (skip if file already ingested)

### 4. RAG retrieval service
- Accept a user query, embed it, perform cosine similarity search against `DocumentChunk` table
- Return top-K most relevant chunks

### 5. Chat service
- Maintain conversation history per session (stored in Postgres)
- Build a system prompt with retrieved context chunks
- Stream LLM responses via `IChatClient`

### 6. Blazor Server UI
- Chat page (`Components/Pages/Chat.razor`) with message bubbles, input box, send button
- Streaming response display
- Basic CSS styling (clean, minimal)

### 7. Program.cs wiring
- Register services (EF Core, ChatService, PdfIngestionService, AI clients)
- Configure Blazor Server
- Trigger PDF ingestion on startup

### 8. Database migration
- Add initial EF Core migration
- Auto-apply on startup

## Notes
- The LLM provider is configurable via `appsettings.json` — works with OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or any OpenAI-compatible API (Ollama, etc.)
- PDF ingestion runs once at startup; re-ingests only new/changed files
- Chat history is persisted per session ID (browser session)
- pgvector handles vector storage and similarity search natively in Postgres
